A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SqueezeAttention. Their complete text, equations, figures, and tables are readable, including v2's added Appendix A. v1 contains no appendix. The retained material can be reliably matched across the layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original layer-similarity measurements, accuracy-versus-cache-budget experiments, memory measurements, and generation throughput results in Sections 3 and 5.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds overhead measurements, hyperparameter sensitivity, task-dependent layer counts, and throughput comparisons in Section 5.5 and Appendix A.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same cosine-similarity measurement, three-cluster K-means grouping, budget-allocation formulas, and decoding procedure. The abstract's new two-group wording does not establish a procedural change: the detailed algorithm still uses three clusters receiving two budget levels.

E1.justification: Appendix A.3 adds LCC code inputs to the layer-importance analysis for Mistral-7B and Llama2-70B. This provides limited new domain coverage, without reporting code-generation accuracy. The original five summarization and question-answering datasets remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Appendix A.4 adds Sliding Window and StreamingLLM as direct throughput comparators, whereas v1's throughput table compares only against Full Cache. These methods already participated in accuracy and memory comparisons; the original comparator memberships remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New evaluation protocols include single-GPU prefilling profiling, a p sweep from 0.1 to 1.0 at a fixed 20% cache budget, and Llama2-7B throughput tests with specified unequal method/baseline budgets. The recommended p range changes from 0.1–0.2 to 0.3–0.4. Section 5.2 also changes baseline-selection wording from per model to per task; unchanged original plots do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: Section 5.5 and Appendix A add substantial analyses of previously untested questions: computational overhead and its components, sensitivity to p, and whether layer importance varies across tasks. The original descriptive similarity heatmaps remain, but v1 lacks these sensitivity and diagnostic studies.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars. The added tables continue reporting point estimates. Appendix A.1's 32 cosine computations correspond to model layers, not independent experimental repetitions.

E6.justification: Tables 4–9 add overhead, sensitivity, layer-count, and throughput results. Examples include prefilling times of 0.636 versus 0.676 seconds, peak sensitivity-test ROUGE-L of 37.69 at p=0.4, and Mistral batch-64 throughput of 682.7 versus 512.2 tokens/s at respective 20% and 30% cache budgets. Original Figures 2–4 and Tables 2–3 retain their values; these are additional findings rather than improved original scores.

T1.justification: The KV-cache equations, cosine-similarity definition, and budget-allocation mathematics are unchanged. Merging the cosine expression into one numbered equation and adding a worked budget example in Appendix A.2 do not introduce new theory, formal assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions claim complementary sequence-wise and layer-wise KV-cache compression, improved accuracy at lower cache budgets, approximately 30–70% memory reductions, and up to 2.2-fold throughput improvement. The expanded abstract and more precise research question retain the same principal contribution and novelty claim.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands the interpretation of when and why the method works. It explains budget starvation at small p, motivates three clusters, discusses amortizing prefilling overhead, and interprets task-dependent layer counts. Section 5.6 adds a concrete applicability limitation: performance depends on an underlying eviction policy that preserves acceptable accuracy.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 newly specifies the profiling workload: cosine comparisons between 8000-by-4096 arrays across 32 layers and K-means clustering of 32 values. Appendix A.2 provides an explicit allocation example and clarifies p's effect. The code-access information and original hardware disclosure are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited-work set is unchanged. The expanded FastGen discussion reiterates the existing distinction between choosing eviction policies and allocating cache budgets; it does not materially revise the claimed relationship to prior work.

P1.justification: v2 makes targeted rewrites to the abstract, research question, and FastGen discussion, standardizes sequence-wise terminology, subdivides the algorithm discussion, and updates author information. Most retained prose and the main section sequence remain stable; the additional scientific sections do not constitute a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column presentation, substantially rearranging text, equations, Algorithm 1, and existing displays. Six tables are added, and several captions and Table 2 headings are revised. All four original figures retain identical underlying graphics.

improvement.justification: The sensitivity tests, overhead measurements, compressed-baseline throughput comparisons, and explicit applicability limitation strengthen the paper's practical evidence. However, the supplementary tests are narrow and incompletely connected to retained results: Appendix A.2's maximum SAMSUM score of 37.69 is not reconciled with Table 2's 41.05 at the same nominal 20% cache budget. The additions support a useful but limited overall improvement.
